description.value: This exploratory study examined resting-state graph-theoretical organization of a 21-node emotion processing and emotion regulation network in women with early life stress who were resilient or susceptible to depression, compared with controls, and examined relationships between network statistics and early life stress severity.
Observational, cross-sectional study of women with early life stress and depression susceptibility or resilience, and controls.

value: The omnibus resiliency group contrast demonstrated decreased degree for the right ventrolateral PFC, decreased clustering and efficiency for the dACC, increased clustering for the right vlPFC, decreased betweenness centrality for the right vlPFC, and altered network organization among resilient individuals.

The strongest group contrast findings suggest altered integration of the right and left vlPFC, dACC, left dlPFC and left amygdala into an emotion processing and emotion regulation network among resilient versus susceptible individuals.
The preliminary results seem to suggest a more distributed pattern of information processing in this network among resilient individuals.
